lengths.full:
Bin Youn is a Korean multimedia artist, researcher, and educator whose practice moves between Seoul, Long Beach, and Ho Chi Minh City, three cities she calls her three waters. She is an Associate Lecturer and Course Coordinator in the School of Communication and Design at RMIT University Vietnam, where she also created rễ-root, an exhibition-centered pedagogical framework replacing traditional portfolio assessment with physical group exhibitions.

Her artistic practice examines displacement, alienation, and technological intimacy through installation, augmented and extended reality, and participatory media. Since 2021 she has developed the Gelora series, in which fallen flowers, preserved with silica gel and scanned, return as hybrid digital creatures activated through touch and East Asian cosmology. Recent iterations include Sacred Tree: Summoning Gelora, a web XR installation structured around the Bagua and Five Directional Colours, and ㅁotherisland, a 5-channel video installation on diasporic identity. Her work has been shown in Vietnam, Malaysia, and the United States, including a Silver and Bronze Award at iNVENTX 2025.

Her research sits at the intersection of East Asian cosmology, cosmotechnics, and diasporic identity, with recent presentations at APARN, ICWL, and TellMe, and forthcoming work at ISEA and ICCM. She holds an MFA in Studio Arts and Photography from California State University Long Beach (2023).

Bin Youn's practice treats displacement as a generative force: alienation opens new forms of connection across boundaries of species, technology, and culture.

paragraphs: Bin Youn is an artist, researcher, and educator whose work explores AI and interactive media as poetic environments connecting cultural memory, ecological relations, and creative learning. Her practice combines installation, XR, and participatory media, alongside research into creative technology education and international collaboration.

Her practice examines displacement, alienation, and technological intimacy through ephemeral encounters, investigating how alienation itself can become a generative force across species, technological, and cultural boundaries.

Bin Youn's research focuses on interactive media environments that investigate relationships between technology, cultural memory, and ecological systems. Her practice combines installation, XR, and AI-driven media with research into creative technology education and participatory learning.
